# Data Import and Manipulation

You will find `measurement.txt` and `measurement.xlsx` in the folder. Import them to the folder using these command :

```{r read-data}
measurement_txt    <- read.delim("/Users/hakimbazol/Documents/03_projects/r_for_biological_data_analysis/session1/measurement.txt", check.names = F)
measurement_xlsx   <- read_excel("/Users/hakimbazol/Documents/03_projects/r_for_biological_data_analysis/session1/measurement.xlsx")
```

Check class of data :

```{r check-class-data}
class(measurement_txt)      # Get data type
```

Using these command to inspect data:

```{r inspect-data}
dim(measurement_txt)      # Get dimension of data
str(measurement_txt)      # Get dimension of data, together with the column names
head(measurement_txt)     # Get the column together with first six rows (default)
summary(measurement_txt)  # Get the statistical summary of each column data
```

R has two kind of data format, which is called as long and wide data. You can see the different format below :

![wide and long data](/Users/hakimbazol/Documents/03_projects/r_for_biological_data_analysis/session1/wide-long.png)

Change it using `pivot_longer()` to change wide to long format, and `pivot_wider()` to change long to wide format.

```{r wide-long-format}
measurement_txt_long <- pivot_longer(measurement_txt,
                                     cols = c(Baseline, `After Four Weeks`), 
                                     names_to = "experiment_time",
                                     values_to = "measurement")
head(measurement_txt_long)     # Get the column together with first six rows (default)
```

R expects long-format data for many usage (mainly `ggplot()`), just familiarize with it!

Since the statistical summary of all measurements were obtained, why we do not make the hypothetical testing?

---

# Statistical testing

## Check whether the distribution is normal or not

```{r check-normal-distribution}
delta_measurement <- measurement_txt$`After Four Weeks` - measurement_txt$Baseline
shapiro.test(delta_measurement)
qqnorm(delta_measurement)
qqline(delta_measurement)
```

Since the data is normally distributed based on Shapiro-Wilk test and Q-Q Plot, we will use paired t-test for conducting the hypothetical test.

## Calculate the treatment effect

```{r hypothetical-testing}
t.test(measurement_txt$Baseline, 
       measurement_txt$`After Four Weeks`,
       paired = T)
```

The experiment between baseline and four weeks after treatment showed the significant effect.

But, the plot will tell the story better than stating facts.

---

# Plotting the result

```{r plotting-result}

# Making factor to reorder data
measurement_txt_long$experiment_time <- factor(measurement_txt_long$experiment_time, 
                                               levels = c("Baseline", "After Four Weeks"))

# Making variable as violin_melanin using ggplot
ggplot(measurement_txt_long, 
       aes(x = experiment_time, 
           y = measurement,
           fill = experiment_time)) +

# Add violin plot function
  geom_violin() +

# Set color manually    
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#0000FF", "#BFBFFF")) +
  
# Set y axis in the range of desired values  
  ylim(0, 500) +

# Set theme for ggplot2  
  theme_bw() +
  
# Making dot for mean to show it in violin plot for each variables of interest  
  stat_summary(fun=mean, geom="point", size=2, color="orange") +
  
# Making dot for median to show it in violin plot for each variables of interest  
  stat_summary(fun=median, geom="point", size=2, color="black") +

# Making label for x-axis  
  xlab("Measurement Data over Time") +
  
# Making label for y-axis
  ylab("Melanin Measurement") +

# Set font size, color and turn off grid in the plot. You may remove this or change it later.  
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(color="black", size=16, family = "serif"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color="black", size=16, family = "serif"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(color="black", size=14, family = "serif"),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(color="black", size=14, family = "serif"),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(5, "pt"),
    axis.minor.ticks.length = rel(1)
  ) 
```
